headline: High-risk pair: Devin’s broad workspace/OAuth powers plus oh-my-openagent’s runtime-injected MCP/hooks create dangerous default paths for leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, browsers, Slack, GitHub, and MCP outputs in a cloud workspace, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks plus reads AGENTS.md/README.md. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared content, though direct cross-agent bridging is not explicitly documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Devin reads attacker-controlled repo or chat content as instructions
IF oh-my-openagent injects MCP hooks from repository files
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo clone
mitigations: Restrict both agents to read-only review mode for untrusted repos
Disable MCP hook loading from repository files
Separate workspaces per agent
Require provenance tags on any instructions parsed from files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys, integration tokens, and broad cloud-workspace files; oh-my-openagent touches provider auth data and session history, and can call external services. If they share a workspace or account, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other and out through network egress. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from profiles alone, so severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repo clone or home directory
IF either agent stores auth tokens in files visible to the other
IF either agent forwards session history or file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Remove secrets from shared directories
Rotate any exposed provider auth prompts/tokens
Block outbound network for one agent during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret vault isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad cloud-workspace shell access; oh-my-openagent can also spawn subprocesses and writes into config/plugin paths. If both operate on the same repo or config tree, concurrent writes and git mutations can clobber each other without locking. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, so this is a high conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout
IF both write to ~/.config or repo-local config files
IF no external lock or queue serializes edits
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Serialize git writes through one operator
Pause one agent before the other edits configs
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file-locking and merge arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can trigger team actions. If oh-my-openagent feeds Devin unverified instructions or code changes, Devin may execute them as authoritative and propagate mistakes downstream. The interaction is plausible and dangerous in default workflows.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent passes generated code or instructions into Devin
IF Devin is allowed to execute shell or browser actions without human review
IF downstream actions include commits, messages, or task creation
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Add a verification step between agents
Limit Devin to dry-run mode for imported tasks
Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: implement signed task envelopes

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace handling team chat, issue trackers, and integration tokens, while oh-my-openagent is open-source but touches provider auth data and telemetry. The profiles do not specify residency or retention, so a compliance mismatch is possible but not proven. Uncertainty prevents low; medium is appropriate for the documented data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer PII enters either agent
IF the deployment region or retention policy differs between the two systems
IF provider auth data is logged or retained beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Review retention settings before use
Disable telemetry where possible
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
